a: Android is Google's mobile operating system used on many phones and tablets.
iOS is Apple's operating system for iPhone and iPad.
Flutter is Google's UI toolkit for building apps for mobile, web, and desktop from one codebase (Dart).
React Native builds mobile apps with React and JavaScript/TypeScript for iOS and Android.
Kotlin is the preferred language for modern Android development.
Swift is Apple's main language for iOS, macOS, and related platforms.
Dart is the programming language used by Flutter.
In Flutter, almost everything is a widget — buttons, layouts, text, and screens.
An APK is the installable package format for Android apps.
An IPA is the installable package format for iOS apps.
Expo is a toolkit that speeds up React Native development and builds.
Google Play Store is the main app store for Android apps.
The Apple App Store is the main app store for iPhone and iPad apps.
A deep link opens a specific screen inside a mobile app from a URL.
Push notifications are messages sent to a device even when the app is in the background.
Firebase is Google's platform for auth, database, messaging, analytics, and hosting.
